39: ARTEMY. Do as you please, Ammos Fiodorovich, I think we ought to try.
38: Enter cautiously, almost on tiptoe, Ammos Fiodorovich, Artemy Filippovich, the Postmaster, Luka Lukich, Dobchinsky and Bobchinsky in full dress-uniform. AMMOS. For God's sake, gentlemen, quick, form your line, and let's have more order. Why, man alive, he goes to Court and rages at the Imperial Council. Draw up in military line, strictly in military line. You, Piotr Ivanovich, take your place there, and you, Piotr Ivanovich, stand here. [Both the Piotr Ivanoviches run on tiptoe to the places indicated.]
37: He goes out on tiptoe, preceded by the Sergeants. SCENE: Same as in Act III.
35: GOVERNOR. Hush! [Puts his hand over Derzhimorda's mouth.] Like a bull bellowing. [Mocking him.] "I had your order—" Makes a noise like an empty barrel. [To Osip.] Go, friend, and get everything ready for your master. And you two, you stand on the steps and don't you dare budge from the spot. And don't let any strangers enter the house, especially the merchants. If you let a single one in, I'll—The instant you see anybody with a petition, or even without a petition and he looks as if he wanted to present a petition against me, take him by the scruff of the neck, give him a good kick, [shows with his foot] and throw him out. Do you hear? Hush—hush!
34: GOVERNOR. Sh—sh! Bandy-legged bears—thumping their boots on the floor! Bump, bump as if a thousand pounds were being unloaded from a wagon. Where in the devil have you been knocking about? DERZHIMORDA. I had your order—
32: ANNA. Come, Mashenka, I'll tell you something I noticed about our guest that I can't tell you unless we are alone together. [They go out.] GOVERNOR. Let them talk away. If you went and listened to them, you'd want to stop up your ears. [To Osip.] Well, friend—
30: GOVERNOR. Hush! [Rises on tip-toe. The rest of the conversation in the scene is carried on in an undertone.] Don't make a noise, for heaven's sake! Go, it's enough.
29: Khlestakov is heard to give a short cough in the next room.
28: ANNA. Come to me, Osip, and I'll give you some, too. MARYA. Osip, darling, kiss your master for me.
26: OSIP. You are too kind, your Excellency. [Puts the money in his pocket.] I'll sure drink your health, sir.
25: GOVERNOR. Very good. You talk sense. I've given you something for tea. Here's something for buns, too.
23: GOVERNOR. Stop now, let me speak. [To Osip.] Tell me, what does your master care for most? I mean, when he travels what does he like? OSIP. As for sights, he likes whatever happens to come along. But what he likes most of all is to be received well and entertained well.
22: ANNA. Listen, Osip, what kind of eyes does your master like most? MARYA. Osip, darling, what a dear nose your master has!
21: OSIP [taking the money.] Thank you, much obliged to you, sir. God grant you health and long life. You've helped a poor man. GOVERNOR. That's all right. I'm glad to do it. Now, friend—
19: GOVERNOR. Enough of your tattle now, really. This is a serious matter, a matter of life and death. (To Osip.) Yes, friend, I like you very much. It's rather chilly now and when a man's travelling an extra glass of tea or so is rather welcome. So here's a couple of rubles for some tea.
17: ANNA. Listen, Osip, does your master wear uniform in St. Petersburg?
15: GOVERNOR. I like your face. You must be a fine man, friend. What—?
14: OSIP. Yes, he likes things to be just so. He insists on things being just so.
13: GOVERNOR. For God's sake, your stupid questions keep a person from getting down to business. Tell me, friend, what sort of a man is your master? Is he strict? Does he rag and bully a fellow—you know what I mean—does he or doesn't he?
11: ANNA. What is your master's rank?
10: GOVERNOR. Do stop now. You just interfere with your silly talk. Well, friend, how—
9: ANNA. Osip, please tell me, how is he—
8: MARYA. Osip, darling, isn't your master just grand?
7: OSIP [aside]. What shall I say? Seeing as they've given me such good feed now, I s'pose they'll do even better later. [Aloud.] Yes, counts do visit him.
6: OSIP. Yes, sir, very good. Thank you kindly. ANNA. Your master has lots of counts and princes visiting him, hasn't he?
5: OSIP. Osip, madam. GOVERNOR [to his wife and daughter]. That'll do, that'll do. [To Osip.] Well, friend, did they give you a good meal?
4: OSIP. No, not yet. He's stretching himself a little. ANNA. What's your name?
3: ANNA. Come here, my good man. GOVERNOR. Hush! Tell me, tell me, is he asleep?
2: The same and Osip. All rush to meet Osip, beckoning to him.
1: ANNA. Leave that to us. Don't bother about that. [Glancing at Marya.] We know a thing or two in that line.
0: The same and the Governor. GOVERNOR. Sh-sh!
